subject: Yearly Site Covariates in the unmarkedMultFrame

messages.author: 960e80f4821bedfb
messages.subject: Yearly Site Covariates in the unmarkedMultFrame
parts:
Hello Group,

Thank you for your help, I greatly appreciate it.  I read the "Dynamic Occupancy Models in Unmarked" guide, which was very useful, but I am seeking a bit of clarification.  When using the colext function in unmarked what should the dimensions of your yearly site covariates be? I have 6 primary sampling periods and 3 secondary sampling periods at 48 sites.  
Therefore, my unmarkedMultFrame should read 

birdoccupancymodel <- unmarkedMultFrame(y = as.matrix(detectionhistory), 
                             siteCovs = SiteCov, 
                             yearlySiteCovs=YearlySiteCovariates,
                             obsCovs=ObserverCovariates, numPrimary=6)

where y = as.matrix(detectionhistory) is a matrix with 48 rows (one for each of my sites) with 18 columns (6 primary sampling periods*3 secondary sampling periods)

siteCovs is a data frame with 48 rows (one for each site) and just as many columns as I have site covariates, so: 48x(the number of site covariates)

yearlySiteCovs is a data frame with 48 rows (one for each site) and each covariate that has one unique observation per season, should have, (in my case) 6 columns because I have 6 primary sampling periods. Since I have 6 primary sampling periods, I believe this means that the covariate will have: 48rows and 6x(The number of covariates) number of columns
  
Then, the obsCovs is a data frame that matches the arrangement of the "y" matrix.  With 48 rows, and 18x(The number of covariates) number of columns.
  The covariates in this data frame have one unique observation for each 0 or 1 entry in my detection history

1) Did I correctly interpret the layout of my files to read into the unmarkedMultFrame?
2) I was especially curious about the yearly covariates, because the crossbill data example had a single yearly site covariate (the year) with rows=number of sites and columns=the number of primary sampling periods
3) Should the yearlySiteCovs have the same layout as the obsCovs?

I apologize for needing clarification in what should be a small matter.  I did read the guide before attempting this, but I would just rest easier having confirmation. 
Thank you in advance for your help,

Evan

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: Yearly Site Covariates in the unmarkedMultFrame
parts:
Evan, the yearlySiteCovs and obsCovs need to be specified as lists, with each item in the list representing a single covariate that was measured at the correct temporal scale (i.e., every primary or secondary occasion).  That is how the model can use multiple covariates at each level:

yearlySiteCovs=list(year=year, climate=climate)
obsCovs=list(date=date, temp=temp)

Each item in those lists is a matrix with dimensions that match either n_sites*n_years or n_sites*n_surveys.  In my example above, year and climate are specific to the primary occasions, while date and temp are specific to the secondary occasions.  And these covariates may or may not vary across sites within the time period.

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: Yearly Site Covariates in the unmarkedMultFrame
parts:
The yearlySiteCovs need to be n_sites*n_years.  Variation can be attributed to sites, years/seasons, and surveys.  Each covariate needs to have n_sites as the first dimension, and then the proper temporal replication as the second dimension: 1 for siteCovs, n_years for yearlySiteCovs, and n_surveys for obsCovs.

The specification in unmarked is designed to be general and flexible, and it would be helpful to think about covariate modeling in terms of the design matrix.
